newsitem.title: ICELAND: Small Icelandic Bourse is put on financial map.
newsitem.headline: Small Icelandic Bourse is put on financial map.

text.p: The Icelandic Stock Exchange (ISE) put itself on the electronic map of international financial centres on Thursday in the hope of attracting more overseas investments to the North Atlantic island.
Under an agreement with Reuters, pages listing stock and bond price movements in the capital of Reykjavik were formally made available on Reuters screens through a live-data feed.

"This is a major milestone for the exchange," ISE President Stefan Halldorsson said. "Foreign investors have been somewhat reluctant to invest in our market because information on market movements has not been readily available."
The ISE was established in 1986 but trading was lacklustre for years because of capital market restrictions.
The market developed quickly following the implementation of the European Economic Area (EEA) agreement in 1993 along with a booming Icelandic economy.
Today ISE has over 300 listed securities, mainly debt instruments, but the number of equities is also growing, now standing at 37 companies.
The introduction of a new electronic trading system last October enabled the bourse to provide live-data feeds to information vendors.

Sigurdur Stefansson, president of VIB, a local investment house that is one of the 16 members of the bourse, forecast some further increase in stock prices in the coming months despite a recent surge.
"However, we might see some correction in the short term which indeed could provide good buying opportunities," he said.
The Icelandic bourse is open 1000-1600 GMT. The feed is available on pages ICSE1 through ICSE9.
